problems.quote: the 50% cap on reservations for Other Backward Classes (OBC) was part of the basic structure
problems.problem: The 50% cap on OBC reservations is a judicial guideline, not a component of the Constitution's basic structure. The Indra Sawhney judgment did not elevate it to basic structure status.
problems.correction: the 50% cap on reservations for Other Backward Classes (OBC) is a judicial guideline, not a basic structure feature
problems.verifierReason: 50% cap is judicial guideline from Indra Sawhney, not basic structure doctrine.

problems.quote: Manohar Lal v Union of India (2017) regarding restrictions on liquor sales
problems.problem: The Supreme Court case that applied the proportionality test to liquor sales restrictions is State of Tamil Nadu v. K. Balu (2017), not Manohar Lal v Union of India.
problems.correction: State of Tamil Nadu v. K. Balu (2017) regarding restrictions on liquor sales
problems.verifierReason: Correct case for highway liquor ban proportionality test is State of Tamil Nadu v. K. Balu (2017).

problems.quote: The Supreme Court referenced DDE in State of U.P. v. Rajesh Gautam (2020) concerning demolition of illegal structures causing incidental loss of livelihood.
problems.problem: The Supreme Court of India has not adopted the Doctrine of Double Effect (DDE) as a legal test; it uses structured proportionality analysis. The cited case either does not exist or does not reference DDE.
problems.correction: The Supreme Court applies proportionality analysis, not DDE, in demolition cases (e.g., Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation, 1985; Ahmedabad Municipal Corp. v. Nawab Khan Gulab Khan, 1997).
problems.verifierReason: The quote invents a 2020 SC case citing DDE; Indian law uses proportionality, not DDE, for demolition/livelihood cases. Correction cites correct doctrine and leading precedents.

problems.quote: "My only brother" implies I am female (since if I were male, I would have a brother and myself are sons)
problems.problem: A male speaker can have an only brother; the phrase does not imply the speaker is female. The reasoning incorrectly assumes gender from the phrase.
problems.correction: "My only brother" does not imply the speaker's gender; a male can have an only brother.
problems.verifierReason: Phrase does not imply speaker's gender; male can have an only brother.

problems.quote: which is the obverse of 'All managers are engineers'
problems.problem: "No non-engineers are managers" is not the obverse of "All managers are engineers"; the obverse is "No managers are non-engineers". The given statement is the converse of that obverse.
problems.correction: which is the converse of the obverse of 'All managers are engineers'
problems.verifierReason: Obverse of 'All M are E' is 'No M are non-E'; 'No non-E are M' is its converse, not the obverse.

problems.quote: Some non‑students are not teachers' is the contrapositive of 'Some teachers are not students'
problems.problem: The contrapositive of "Some teachers are not students" (O) is "Some non-students are not non-teachers", not "Some non-students are not teachers".
problems.correction: Some non‑students are not non‑teachers' is the contrapositive of 'Some teachers are not students'
problems.verifierReason: Contrapositive of O proposition 'Some T are not S' is 'Some non-S are not non-T', not 'Some non-S are not T'.

problems.quote: The algorithm guarantees completeness for the Boolean fragment because Euler diagrams are isomorphic to the set‑theoretic models of categorical logic.
problems.problem: The described algorithm (shading zones, placing X-marks) is the Venn diagram method, not Euler diagrams. Euler diagrams do not use shading or exhaustive zones; Venn diagrams are the ones isomorphic to set-theoretic models for Boolean categorical logic.
problems.correction: The algorithm guarantees completeness for the Boolean fragment because Venn diagrams are isomorphic to the set‑theoretic models of categorical logic.
problems.verifierReason: Shading/X-marks algorithm is Venn diagram method; Venn (not Euler) diagrams are isomorphic to Boolean set-theoretic models.

problems.quote: Advanced puzzles may embed circular references (e.g., “A’s grandson is B’s father”).
problems.problem: The example “A’s grandson is B’s father” is not a circular reference; it describes a linear generational relationship (A → child → grandson = B’s father). A circular reference requires a closed loop (e.g., “A is B’s father and B is A’s father”).
problems.correction: Advanced puzzles may embed circular references (e.g., “A is B’s father and B is A’s father”).
problems.verifierReason: Original example is linear (A→child→grandson→B), not circular. Correction provides a valid closed-loop example (A→B→A).

problems.quote: the correct average is the harmonic mean weighted by the times spent at each speed
problems.problem: Average speed for a journey with two constant speeds over given times is the arithmetic mean weighted by time (total distance/total time), not the harmonic mean weighted by time.
problems.correction: the correct average is the arithmetic mean weighted by the times spent at each speed
problems.verifierReason: Average speed given times is time-weighted arithmetic mean (total distance/total time); harmonic mean weighted by time is incorrect.

problems.quote: ¬R → ¬(Q → P) which simplifies to ¬R → (Q ∧ ¬P)
problems.problem: This is not the correct contrapositive of the nested implication P → (Q → R). The contrapositive of P → (Q → R) is ¬(Q → R) → ¬P, which simplifies to (Q ∧ ¬R) → ¬P.
problems.correction: The contrapositive of P → (Q → R) is (Q ∧ ¬R) → ¬P.
problems.verifierReason: Quote gives wrong contrapositive; correction gives correct (Q∧¬R)→¬P.

problems.quote: events with zero slack lie on every critical path
problems.problem: In the Critical Path Method, an event with zero slack (float) lies on at least one critical path, not necessarily on every critical path. There can be multiple critical paths, and a zero-slack event belongs to one of them.
problems.correction: events with zero slack lie on at least one critical path
problems.verifierReason: Zero-slack events lie on at least one critical path, not necessarily all.

problems.quote: for |r| n≥0 n rⁿ = r/(1−r)²
problems.problem: The condition for convergence is missing and the summation index is garbled; the formula for ∑ n rⁿ is incorrectly attached to the condition for ∑ rⁿ.
problems.correction: for |r|<1, ∑ n rⁿ = r/(1−r)²
problems.verifierReason: Original missing convergence condition and garbled summation; correction supplies |r|<1 and correct ∑ notation, accurate.

problems.quote: Cardinal direction calculi (e.g., the 9‑intersection model or the more expressive OPRA m )
problems.problem: The 9-intersection model is a topological relation model (Egenhofer), not a cardinal direction calculus.
problems.correction: Cardinal direction calculi (e.g., the cardinal direction calculus or the more expressive OPRA_m)
problems.verifierReason: 9-intersection model is topological (Egenhofer), not cardinal direction; correction gives valid example.

problems.quote: M1 adds demand deposits of the public with commercial banks and other deposits with the RBI
problems.problem: M0 already includes other deposits with the RBI; M1 does not simply add them but comprises currency with public, demand deposits, and other deposits with RBI.
problems.correction: M1 comprises currency with public, demand deposits with commercial banks, and other deposits with RBI
problems.verifierReason: Original omits currency with public; correction matches standard M1 definition.

problems.quote: it is used mainly for converting nominal GDP into real GDP at factor cost
problems.problem: WPI is not used for converting nominal GDP to real GDP; the GDP deflator is used for that purpose.
problems.correction: it is used mainly for indexing government contracts and wholesale price analysis
problems.verifierReason: WPI is not used for GDP deflation; correction correctly states its main uses.

problems.quote: The Reserve Bank of India, as the chair of the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC)
problems.problem: The FSDC is chaired by the Union Finance Minister, not the RBI.
problems.correction: The Reserve Bank of India, as a member of the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC)
problems.verifierReason: FSDC is chaired by the Finance Minister; RBI is only a member.

problems.quote: in the August 2022 meeting the external members voted for a 50‑basis‑point hike while the Governor and Deputy Governor favoured a 35‑basis‑point increase; the majority carried the larger hike
problems.problem: The August 2022 MPC meeting was unanimous for a 50 bps hike; there was no split vote between external and internal members.
problems.correction: in the August 2022 meeting all members voted for a 50‑basis‑point hike
problems.verifierReason: August 2022 MPC vote was unanimous for a 50‑bps hike.

problems.quote: Gond painting, once executed on house walls during the Bhagoria festival, entered the international art market after the 2003 “Gond Art Exhibition” at the Musée
problems.problem: Musée du Quai Branly opened in 2006; no 2003 exhibition there.
problems.correction: Gond painting, once executed on house walls during the Bhagoria festival, entered the international art market after the 2003 “Gond Art Exhibition” in Paris
problems.verifierReason: Musée du Quai Branly opened 2006, so 2003 exhibition there impossible; correction "in Paris" avoids error and is accurate.
